claim: The Government of India's own gazette calls Sanjay Gandhi National Park 'a unique habitat enclosed in the metropolis of Mumbai', located in Thane and Mumbai districts.

evidence.locator: S.O. 229(E) draft notification, first WHEREAS clause (txt line ~1479-1481)
evidence.quote: is a unique habitat enclosed in the metropolis of Mumbai and is located in the Thane and Mumbai District of Maharashtra

note: So 'inside the city' is the government's wording for the metropolis; the park spans two districts (Mumbai Suburban and Thane), not Mumbai city alone.

claim: The park as administered today covers 103.84 sq km.

evidence.quote: to make the 103.84 sq.km. of SGNP known today

method: method/sgnp_boundary_area.py: straight-line polygon through the 12 gazette boundary points gives ~122 km2 and a 22 km north-south extent; a rough cross-check only (straight chords overstate a winding boundary).
note: Other official figures exist (86.96 sq km notified; 103.68 administrative, in MoEF ESZ committee minutes examined but not cited, lite cap). Say 'about 104 sq km' or 'over 100 sq km'.

claim: Vihar and Tulsi lakes were built by the British government to supply drinking water to Mumbai; the park's timeline dates this to 1870.

evidence.locator: History of SGNP, timeline slide 1 (carousel index 0 = '1870', sgnp_history.html)
evidence.quote: Vihar and Tulsi lakes were constructed by the British government to supply drinking water to Mumbai city.

evidence.locator: S.O. 229(E), Annexure I boundary points table

method: Year-to-caption pairing read from carousel indices in sgnp_history.html (data-slide-to 0 = 1870 = first slide).
note: Gazette confirms the lakes sit at the park edge and that MCGM uses them as reservoirs; the 1870 date is the park's own and is single-source. Say 'in the 1800s' or 'from 1870, says the park'.

claim: The Bombay Municipal Corporation acquired the two lakes' catchment areas and added land from the Aarey government dairy to protect it (timeline: 1942) - the water supply is why the forest was kept.

evidence.locator: History of SGNP, timeline slide 2 (carousel index 1 = '1942')
evidence.quote: The Bombay Municipal Corporation acquired the catchment areas of these two lakes and also added the land from the government dairy of Aarey to protect it.

evidence.locator: S.O. 229(E), ESZ regulated activities table, MCGM reservoirs entry (txt line ~1744)
evidence.quote: purpose of MCGM for their existing reservoirs of tulsi

note: The causal 'why' is the park manager's narrative order (lakes -> catchment protected -> national park); hedge as 'the park's own history says'.

claim: It began as Krishnagiri National Park, about 20 sq km, under the Bombay National Park Act (timeline 1950); 68.27 sq km was declared Borivali National Park (timeline 1968); it was renamed Sanjay Gandhi National Park in 1981 and enlarged with Thane forests.

evidence.quote: The Krishnagiri National Park, covering an area of about 20 sq km was established under the Bombay National Park Act.
An area of 68.27 sq.km. was declared formally as the Borivali National Park.
In 1981, it was re-dedicated as 'Sanjay Gandhi National Park' in memory of Sanjay Gandhi

note: The same page's prose gives 1969 for the expansion and 1974 for Krishnagiri (conflicts.md K1, K2). Safe: '1981 rename' (both agree). Hedge the earlier years.

claim: The Kanheri Buddhist caves sit inside the park, and the park's first name echoes them: 'Kanheri' derives from Sanskrit 'Krishnagiri', 'black mountain'.

evidence.quote: The word 'Kanheri' is derived from Sanskrit word 'Krishnagiri', which literally means 'black mountain'.
A 2,000-year-old complex sits within the park

evidence.locator: S.O. 229(E), Annexure I boundary points table, point 18

note: The cave count is NOT safe: the Kanheri page itself reads 'more than 100 (is this correct) caves'. Do not say a number. ASI record not opened (lite cap).

claim: Camera traps detected 54 adult leopards and 4 cubs in the park in 2024 (52 adults and 6 cubs in 2023).

evidence.quote: 52 adult leopard individuals and six cubs were detected in SGNP in 2023, followed by 54 adult leopard individuals and four cubs in 2024.

note: These are photographed individuals (minimum count), not a total estimate. Say 'at least 54 adult leopards were photographed'.

claim: A 2015 scat study found domestic animals made up 43% of SGNP leopards' diet, stray dogs 24%.

evidence.quote: domestic prey contributed 43% of the leopard's diet in SGNP, with stray dogs accounting for 24%

note: Attribution to Nikit Surve's 2015 study as reported by the Forest Department; the study itself not opened (lite cap).

claim: In 2016 the Ministry proposed an Eco-sensitive Zone of 6110.629 hectares, up to four kilometres from the park boundary.

evidence.quote: The Eco-Sensitive Zone is spread over an area of 6110.629

note: Draft figure; final S.O. 3645(E) of 5 Dec 2016 referenced by the 2020 amendment but not opened. Say 'proposed'.

claim: The Forest Department says leopards share the SGNP landscape with an estimated 20,925 people per sq km (2011 census).

evidence.locator: Living with Leopards page, 'Mumbaikars for SGNP' para 2
evidence.quote: along with an estimated 20,925 people per sq. km (according to the 2011 census)

note: Basis (which area) not stated; not checked against Census tables (lite cap). Attribution only, keep off screen as a hard number.
